A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GS-LVMOGP research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original GS-LVMOGP experiments on exchange rates, NYC crime, temperature, USHCN and spatial transcriptomics, including quantitative predictions and gene-clustering results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a synthetic mini-batch study and evaluated baselines.

M1.justification: The covariance model, variational parameterization, stochastic inference and prediction approaches remain unchanged. The added 1/J factor reconciles the displayed training estimator with Monte Carlo averaging already specified in v1 Equation 16; it does not establish a different implemented procedure.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix A.6.1 adds a controlled synthetic regression dataset with 100 outputs. All five real-world applications, including prediction at unseen spatial locations, remain covered.

E2.justification: V2 adds HetMOGP to the Exchange comparison in Table 1 and independent Poisson SVGPs to NYC Table 2. The timing comparison against ST-SVGP, MF-ST-SVGP and SVGP-1500/3000 in v1 Table 11 disappears, although their predictive comparisons remain in v2 Table 12.

E3.justification: The synthetic experiment introduces 100 inputs per output, a 50/50 training/test split and nine input/output batch configurations. Added baseline settings include HetMOGP latent-function counts 1–5 and 1,000 inducing points per independent SVGP. The stated SMSE formula is corrected; existing real-data splits and training budgets remain unchanged, with no documented rerun attributable to that correction.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix A.6.1, Figure 4 and Table 7 add a substantive investigation of mini-batch sensitivity through convergence trajectories, runtime and predictive performance, directly testing the stochastic optimization approach. Table 9 adds HetMOGP sensitivity to latent-function count. Conversely, v1's comparative NYC runtime analysis is removed; existing Q comparisons and OILMM sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Existing benchmarks retain five-seed repetitions or five-fold cross-validation and standard-deviation reporting. Revised dispersion values in Tables 3–4 are result changes; neither an increased run count nor a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure is stated.

E6.justification: V2 adds synthetic convergence, timing and prediction results, HetMOGP Exchange scores of 0.92 SMSE and -1.3 NLPD, and NYC I-SVGP-1000 scores of 3.000 RMSE and 1.939 NLPD. Existing main-table means remain unchanged, but reported standard deviations in Tables 3–4 change materially: USHCN Q=3 MSE remains 0.618 while its deviation changes from 0.0062 to 0.08. V1 Table 11's timing results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 restores the missing 1/J normalization in the doubly stochastic ELBO displayed in Section 3.3. It also corrects SMSE from v1 Equation 55 to the ratio of input-averaged squared errors in v2 Equation 45. The principal variational, KL and predictive-moment derivations otherwise remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain stochastic LV-MOGP inference with input/output mini-batching, multiple latent components and support for Gaussian and non-Gaussian likelihoods. V2's explicit emphasis on at least 5,000 outputs and expanded conclusion elaborate capabilities already claimed and demonstrated in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explains faster convergence per epoch with smaller batches through more frequent optimization updates and discusses batch-size tradeoffs. It adds an explicit inducing-variable bottleneck and explains how latent-variable integration mitigates overfitting. The earlier Q>1 computational limitation survives in Section 3.3 despite removal of the standalone limitations section.

D1.justification: V2 adds a GS-LVMOGP code-repository link and dataset-specific kernel and latent-variable initialization details in Appendix A.6 and Table 6. Sections 3.4 and A.5 explicitly identify latent-mean prediction as the experimental procedure and the moment-matching alternative as unused. Existing hardware and training-budget disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 4 replaces the brief scalability-focused review with substantially broader coverage of convolutional, spectral, neural-embedding, autoregressive and SDE-based MOGPs. Appendix A.4 adds a substantive comparison with neural processes. Several single-output scalability references disappear, while the earlier ICM/LMC relationship is developed in the main text.

P1.justification: The main section order and most technical exposition remain intact. Changes include language cleanup, revised front matter, expanded background and conclusion, rewritten related work and reorganized appendix subsections. Some cross-references become stale, including references to the predictive Equation 13 and reordered Figure 3 panels.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document: Tables 3–4 become larger stacked displays, Figure 3 panels are reordered, and appendix prediction plots move. It adds initialization, synthetic-results and HetMOGP tables plus a convergence figure, while removing v1's model-summary and runtime tables. Most existing prediction and clustering graphics retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The controlled mini-batch study and additional baselines strengthen targeted validation of the existing method. Corrected formulas, initialization disclosures, code-access information and broader research context improve scrutiny and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed NYC timing comparison, although unexplained standard-deviation revisions and stale cross-references limit the overall improvement.
